BURHAN:v3p194/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.claim: The narrative omits that the messenger took and delivered the letter; the Queen's response shows that intervening action.
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ﴾ 1 الآية فأعقب بقوله حكاية عنها ﴿ قالت يا أيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p146/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī's first type, concision by reduction, packs the letter's heading, content, and request into the few words of Solomon's message.
ITQAN:v3p146/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي في التبيان الإيجاز الخالي من الحذف ثلاثة أقسام أحدها إيجاز القصر وهو أن يقصر اللفظ على معناه كقوله

ITQAN:v3p146/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.claim: The author notes that calling a rhetorician's words molds for his meaning treats equality of wording and meaning as concision too.
ITQAN:v3p146/r5.anchor: وقيل في وصف بليغ كانت ألفاظه قوالب معناه قلت وهذا رأي من يدخل المساواة في الإيجاز

ELMALILI:27:21-31/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r14.claim: The queen calls the delivered letter important and deserving of reverence.
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r14.anchor: bana bir mektub bırakıldı bana, çok mühim ve şâyân-ı tekrîm

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.claim: To verify the hoopoe's report, Solomon sent a letter with it to the queen and instructed it to return with her response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.anchor: yazdığı bir mektubu kraliçeye götürüp sonuçtan kendisini haberdar etmesini hüdhüde emretti.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r5.claim: The queen and courtiers’ lack of amazement suggests that delivery of royal letters through birds was customary at least among kings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r5.anchor: Neither did she express amazement nor her courtiers when the letter was received.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r6.claim: Calling the letter honourable shows that the queen and courtiers already esteemed Solomon; Islahi says the Torah, Talmud, and later Qur’anic verses also indicate this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r6.anchor: This shows that she and her courtiers already held Solomon (sws) in high esteem.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.claim: The queen summarized the letter as being from Solomon and beginning in God’s name, rather than reading it all aloud.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r7.anchor: the letter is from Solomon (sws) and begins with the name of the merciful God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.claim: Since the queen only summarized the letter, she named its sender and opening; ancient royal letters and decrees conventionally began by naming sender and recipient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r1.anchor: for this reason she only told them the name of the sender and the manner in which it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p481/r4.claim: Although she summarized it, ancient letters were concise, as Prophet Muhammad’s letters show, so Solomon’s letter may have contained only the words she reported.

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r1.claim: Bilqis addresses her leading people, whose number is given as either 313 or twelve thousand.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r1.anchor: لأشراف قومها وهم ثلاثمائة وثلاثة عشر أو اثنا عشر ألفا

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r2.claim: The ملأ are the community's dignitaries, who fill eyes with awe and hearts with majesty; their plural is أملاء.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r2.anchor: والملأ عظماء القوم الذين يملؤون العيون مهابة والقلوب جلالة جمعه أملاء

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r3.claim: She calls the letter noble because it is honored by her, sealed with a remarkable seal, and delivered in an unusual manner.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r3.anchor: مكرم على معظم لدي لكونه مختوما بخاتم عجيب وأصلا على نهج غير معتاد

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r4.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r4.claim: Al-As'ila al-Muqahima says Solomon's miracle was in his ring: sealing with it displayed his sovereignty and cast fear into Bilqis's heart.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r4.anchor: معجزة سليمان كانت في خاتمه فختم الكتاب بالخاتم الذي فيه ملكه

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r5.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that a letter's nobility lies in its seal.

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r6.claim: A version from Ibn Abbas adds the verse in which Bilqis calls the letter noble; al-Sakhawi records it in al-Maqasid al-Hasana.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس بزيادة وهو قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r7.speaker: أنس
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r7.claim: Anas reports that Muhammad adopted a silver seal ring engraved Muhammad, Messenger of God, because non-Arabs would not accept an unsealed letter.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r7.anchor: على ما رواه أنس رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r8.claim: A saying warns that an unsealed letter is defeated.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r8.anchor: ويقال : كل كتاب لا يكون مختوما فهو مغلوب

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r9.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r9.claim: Jalalayn interprets noble as meaning that the letter's contents are good.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r9.anchor: كريم أي حسن ما فيه انتهى

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r10.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh offers two senses: pleasing in wording and meaning, or noble because it begins with the basmala.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r10.anchor: كما قال ابن الشيخ في أوائل سورة الشعراء : كتاب كريم أي مرضي في لفظه ومعانيه

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r11.claim: An anonymous couplet praises God's name as the best opening for a letter and as adornment of names and comfort for hearts.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r11.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : (ون مضمون نامه نام خداوند بوده

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r12.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r12.claim: The Najmiyya reading says Bilqis called the letter noble because it led her to guidance and faith in the Presence of the Generous.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r12.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن الكتاب لما كان

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r13.claim: Some say honoring the letter brought Bilqis guidance, as the magicians gained faith by showing Moses proper respect.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r13.anchor: قال بعضهم : لاحترامها الكتاب رزقت الهداية حتى آمنت كالسحرة لما قدموا في قولهم

BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r14.claim: When Khosrow tore the Prophet's letter, God tore apart his kingdom as punishment for disbelief and defiance.
BURSEVI:v6p249#2/r14.anchor: ولما مزق كسرى كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مزق الله ملكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r11.claim: Bilqis takes the letter and summons the leaders of her people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r11.anchor: فأخذت الكتاب ونادت أشراف قومها: قالت يا أيها الملأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r12.claim: The letter is called noble because it was sealed with a stamp.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r1.speaker: الحديث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r1.claim: A hadith says a letter is ennobled by its seal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r1.anchor: وفي الحديث: «كرم الكتاب ختمه» أو لكونه من سليمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r2.claim: One explanation for the letter's nobility is that it came from Solomon, whose sovereignty Bilqis knew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r2.anchor: أو لكونه من سليمان، وكانت عالمة بملكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r3.claim: Another explanation is that a bird carried it, so she thought it might be a heavenly message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r3.anchor: أو لكون الرسول به الطير، فظنته كتابا سماويا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r4.claim: Another explanation is its gentle, mild tone, without insult or anything that would provoke resentment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r4.anchor: أو لكونه تضمن لطفا ولينا، لا سبا ولا ما يغير النفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the letter began with God's name.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r6.claim: Bilqis first identifies the letter's sender and then explains its contents, moving from an unspecified report to its interpretation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r7.claim: Her passive wording ألقي leaves the deliverer unnamed, either because she did not know who cast it or to belittle the bird if she saw it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p234/r7.anchor: وفي بنائها ألقي للمفعول دلالة على جهلها بالملقي، حيث حذفته، أو تحقيرا له

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r1.claim: She speaks after the hoopoe delivers the letter and withdraws as ordered; omission signals prompt obedience and leaves the obvious unstated.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r1.anchor: وإنما طوي ذكره إيذانا بكمال مسارعته إلى إقامة ما أمر به من الخدمة واشعارا بالاستغناء عن التصريح به لغاية ظهوره

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r2.speaker: رُوي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r2.claim: One report says Solomon perfumed and sealed the letter, sent it with the hoopoe, who found the queen asleep in Ma'rib; she locked the doors and kept keys under her head, and he entered through a window and placed it on her chest.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r2.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام كتب كتابه وطبعه بالمسك وختمه بخاتمه ودفعه إلى الهدهد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r3.claim: Another account places the letter between her breasts; another says the hoopoe pecked her awake in fright.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r3.anchor: وفي رواية بين ثدييها وقيل : نقرها فانتبهت فزعة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r4.claim: One account says the hoopoe arrived among the queen's leaders and soldiers, hovered until she looked up, then dropped the letter into her lap; seeing the seal made her tremble and submit.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r4.anchor: وقيل أتاها والقادة والجنود حواليها فرفرف ساعة والناس ينظرون حتى رفعت رأسها فالقى الكتاب في حجرها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r5.claim: Another account says she worshipped the sun through a window; the hoopoe blocked its light with its wings, she rose, and it delivered the letter.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r5.anchor: وقيل : كانت في البت كوة تقع الشمس منها كل يوم فاذا نظرت اليها سجدت فجاء الهدهد فسدها بجناحيه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r6.claim: The queen was said to be literate in Arabic, descended from Ya'rub ibn Qahtan, and famously from Tubba al-Himyari.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r6.anchor: وكانت قارئة كاتبة عربية من نسل يعرب بن قحطان واشتهر أنها من نسل تبع الحميري

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r7.claim: The Himyari script was highly refined under the Tubba kings, called musnad with separate letters; Himyar restricted its teaching and Mudar learned it from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r7.anchor: وكان الخط العربي في غاية الاحكام والاتقان والجودة في دولة التبابعة وهو المسمى بالخط الحميري وكان بحمير كتابة تسمى المسند حروفها مفصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r8.speaker: ابن خلدون
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r8.claim: Ibn Khaldun preferred the view that Arabic writing was learned from the Tubba people and Himyar of Hira, then passed to the people of the Hijaz.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r8.anchor: واختار ابن خلدون القول بأنه تعلم الكتابة العربية من التبابعة وحمير أهل الحيرة وتعلمها منهم أهل الحجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r9.claim: The queen's apparent Arab identity and her reading of the letter suggest it was Arabic; Solomon may have known Arabic or had a multilingual interpreter as kings often did.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r9.anchor: وظاهر كون بلقيس من العرب وأنها قرأت الكتاب يقتضي أن الكتاب كان عربيا ولعل سليمان عليه السلام كان يعرف العربي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r10.claim: Alternatively, Solomon's letter may have been in his own language and script, with a translator informing the queen of its contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الكتاب غير عربي بلغة سليمان عليه السلام وقلمه وكان قلمه كما نقل عن الامام أحمد البوني كاهنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r11.claim: She assembled her people's notables and consulted them, as the next verse narrates.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194/r11.anchor: فجمعت أشراف قومها وأخبرتهم بذلك واستشارتهم كما حكى سبحانه عنها بقوله جل وعلا قالت : ( يا أيها الملؤا إني القي إلي كتاب كريم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r1.claim: Solomon may have used the language of the land since the hoopoe said the queen had been given everything and a translator was among a king's needs; fittingly he would keep his own tongue.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r1.anchor: وأقدم سليمان عليه السلام على كتابة الكتاب اليها كذلك قول الهدهد ( وأوتيت من كل شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r2.claim: She may have known the script herself and read the letter; the author favors a non-Arabic letter because writing in Arabic would imply Solomon already knew her circumstances.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r2.anchor: ورجح احتمال أن يكون الكتاب غير عربي بأن الكتابة لها بالعربية تستدعي الوقوف على حالها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r3.claim: The counterargument is that the hoopoe's report identified Saba as Arab, and Solomon would know its queen was likely Arab.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r3.anchor: وتعقب بانه دله على كونها عربية قول الهدهد ( جئتك من سبأ بنبأ يقين إني وجدت امرأة تملكهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وزهير بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r4.claim: They interpret كريم as sealed, supporting the recommendation to seal a letter for its noble content or sender.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r4.anchor: وقد فسر ابن عباس وقتادة وزهير بن محمد ( الكريم ) هنا بالمختوم وفيه كما قيل استحباب ختم الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r5.speaker: حديث
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r5.claim: A report says the honor of a letter is its seal; the author cites this for sealing correspondence.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r5.anchor: ففي الحديث كرم الكتاب ختمه وفي شرح أدب الكاتب يقال أكرمت الكتاب فهو كريم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r6.speaker: ابن المقنع
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Muqaffa says that whoever writes a letter to a brother but does not seal it has treated him lightly.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن المقنع : من كتب إلى أخيه كتابا ولم يختمه فقد استخف به

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r7.claim: The letter's nobility may reflect its honored content, its sender's rank and royal seal, its bird messenger, its opening with God's name, or its unusual arrival.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r7.anchor: أو لكرم مرسلهمرسله وعلو منزلته وعلمت ذلك بالسماع أو بكون كتابه مختوما باسمه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is that the queen thought the letter divine because a bird delivered it; the author dismisses this.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : أن ذلك لظنها إياه بسبب أن الملقي له طيرا أنه كتاب سماوي وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r9.claim: The passive form أُلقي omits the agent because the agent was unimportant, unknown to her, or deemed insignificant.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r9.anchor: وبناء ( القي ) للمفعول لعدم الاهتمام بالفاعل وقيل : لجهلها به أو لكونه حقيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r10.claim: In the Fusūs, Ibn Arabi says the queen deliberately omitted who delivered the letter to show her court access to matters by unknown means, a political tactic that earned her precedence.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r10.anchor: وقال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره في الفصوص : من حكمة بلقيس كونها لم تذكر من ألقى اليها الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p194#2/r11.claim: The emphatic opening marks the importance of the judgment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r8.claim: Bilqis could read; seeing the seal made her tremble and submit because she recognized the seal as a sign of Solomon’s greater sovereignty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r8.anchor: وكانت قارئة، فلما رأت الخاتم أرعدت وخضعت لأن ملك سليمان كان في خاتمه، وعرفت أن الذي أرسل الكتاب إليها أعظم ملكا منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r9.claim: The hoopoe waited nearby while Bilqis sat on her throne and summoned her council, said to number 12,000 commanders each leading 100,000 fighters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r9.anchor: وتأخر الهدهد غير بعيد، فجاءت حتى قعدت على سرير مملكتها وجمعت الملأ من قومها، وهم اثنا عشر ألف قائد مع كل قائد مائة ألف مقاتل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Bilqis had 100,000 qils, each with 100,000 men; a qil was a king subordinate to the supreme monarch.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: كان مع بلقيس مائة ألف [قيل، مع كل قيل مائة ألف] والقيل الملك دون الملك الأعظم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r11.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r11.claim: They say her council consisted of 313 men, each commanding 10,000.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r12.claim: “She said” refers to Bilqis, and “the council” means the leading and eminent people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r12.anchor: {قالت} هم بلقيس: {يا أيها الملأ} وهم أشراف الناس وكبراؤهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r1.speaker: عطاء والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r1.claim: They say Bilqis called the letter noble because it was sealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r1.anchor: قال عطاء والضحاك: سمته كريما لأنه كان مختوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted from the Prophet, says that a letter’s dignity lies in its seal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "كرامة الكتاب ختمه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r3.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r3.claim: They interpret “noble letter” as a good or beautiful letter; al-Zajjaj chooses this view, meaning its contents were good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: "كتاب كريم" أي: حسن، وهو اختيار الزجاج، وقال: حسن ما فيه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says “noble” refers to the honor of the letter’s sender.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: "كريم"، أي: شريف لشرف صاحبه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r5.claim: Another explanation is that Bilqis called it noble because it began with “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p159/r5.anchor: وقيل: سمته كريما لأنه كان مصدرا ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r3.claim: The letter is noble because of its content or sender, because it was sealed, or because its arrival was wondrous: the hoopoe entered her locked house through a window and dropped it on her neck while she reclined unaware.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r3.anchor: لكرم مضمونه أو مرسله، أو لأنه كان

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r1.claim: The noble book is described as sealed and ornamented; other explanations locate its nobility in its opening with the basmala, its seal, or its title.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r1.anchor: قال مختوم مزين بزينته ، وقيل : فيه كرامة الكتاب ابتداؤه

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r2.claim: One view says the book's honor lies in its opening with the basmala.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : فيه كرامة الكتاب ابتداؤه ' بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم '

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r3.claim: Another view says the book's honor lies in its seal.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : كرامته ختمه وقيل كرامته عنوانه

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r4.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r4.claim: Husayn compares saying basmala to God's command Be: rightly invoking God's name makes things real, as God's command Be brings them into being.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r4.anchor: وقال الحسين : بسم الله منك بمنزلة كن منه فإذا احسنت أن تقول : بسم الله تحققت الأشياء

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r5.speaker: ابن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r5.claim: Ibn Tahir says the Pen wrote the events destined until Resurrection beginning with the basmala, meaning all things are purified through God alone.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن طاهر : لما قال الله للقلم اكتب . قال : ما اكتب قال : اكتب ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r6.speaker: ابن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r6.claim: Bilqis called the letter noble because it opened as the Preserved Tablet did, and only a noble person begins written correspondence.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r6.anchor: فلما رأت بلقيس كتابه مفتتحا بما افتتح به اللوح المحفوظ قالت : ^ ( هذا كتاب كريم ) ^

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r7.claim: One reader calls the book blessed because it captures the heart so fully that only submission, not answer or speech, remains possible.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : كتاب كريم أي مبارك على اخذ بجوامع قلبي فليس لي عنه جواب

SULAMI:v2p89#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r8.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r8.claim: Qasim says honoring the book brought Bilqis guidance, faith, and affirmation; reverence can confer blessings on people even after time has passed.
SULAMI:v2p89#3/r8.anchor: قال القاسم : لاحترامها الكتاب وتعظيمها له رزقت الهداية حتى آمنت وصدقت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r3.claim: The Queen gathers her people, or perhaps only the notables, before speaking; the author also says she was literate and from the people of Tubbaʿ.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r4.claim: The passive phrase saying that a letter was cast to her presents its delivery as strange and unexpected.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r4.anchor: فبنت للمفعول قولها : { إني ألقي إلي } أي بإلقاء ملق على وجه غريب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r5.claim: She calls the letter noble because of the distinction of sender and messenger, its opening with God's greatest name, its brevity, and its complete meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r5.anchor: منجهة المرسل والرسول والافتتاح بالاسم الأعظم إلى ما له من وجازة اللفظ وبلوغ المعنى

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r10.claim: Qatada recounts that the hoopoe entered through a window while the queen slept, dropped the letter on her, and that she called its contents good.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r10.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كانت صاحبة سبأ إذا رقدت غلقت الأبواب وأخذت المفاتيح فوضعتها تحت رأسها

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the “noble letter” as sealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس {إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم} قال: مختوم

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r12.speaker: زهير بن محمد
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r12.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says “noble letter” means sealed; kings seal their letters and accept no letter without a seal.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r12.anchor: عن زهير بن محمد في قوله {كتاب كريم} قال: تريد مختوم وكذلك الملوك تختم كتبها لا تجيز بينها كتابا إلا بخاتم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Solomon's queen had one thousand chiefs, each commanding one hundred thousand.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في صاحبة سليمان وكان تحتها الف قيل كل قيل على مائة الف

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r2.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r2.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says the queen addressed her people when she called, “O chiefs.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r2.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد قال : ثم قالت يا ايها الملا تريد قومها .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r3.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r3.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman says that after reading a letter unlike those of earlier kings, the queen summoned Yemen's leaders.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، عن يزيد بن رومان ، قال : فلما قرات سمعت كتابا ليس من كتب الملوك التي كانت قبلها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the hoopoe dropped Solomon's letter at the queen's throne, where it was read aloud and identified as from Solomon with the basmala.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فانطلق بالكتاب حتى اذا توسط عرشها ، القى الكتاب اليها فقرئ عليها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the hoopoe released the letter from high above into the queen's lap; she thought it came from God and feared it before reading it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي اني القي الي كتاب كريم فانطلق الهدهد ، فارتفع حتى تغيب في السماء حذاها ، ثم ارسل الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says the queen sensed that the letter was noble and felt apprehensive when it was delivered, so she addressed her chiefs.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس يا ايها الملا اني القي الي كتاب كريم قال : فلما القى الكتاب اليها سقط في خلدها انه كتاب كريم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r1.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r1.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says “noble” means sealed: kings seal their letters and exchange no letter without a seal.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r1.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد في قول الله : اني القي الي كتاب كريم اشفقت منه تريد مختوم ، وكذلك الملوك تختم كتبها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r2.claim: Qatada says “noble” means that the letter's contents were good.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2872/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : اني القي الي كتاب كريم قال : يقول حسن ما فيه

FARRA:v2p291/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p291/r6.claim: The letter is called noble because it was sealed, according to what Farrāʾ was told.

FARRA:v2p291/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r7.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v2p291/r7.claim: Another account says the queen called it noble because she had seen a king’s letter and associated nobility with its author.
FARRA:v2p291/r7.anchor: وصفت الكتاب بالكرم لقومها لأنها رأت كتاب ملك عندها

FARRA:v2p291/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p291/r8.claim: He rejects the suggestion that she called it noble before learning it was from Solomon, since she had read it before leaving for her council.
FARRA:v2p291/r8.anchor: قبل أن تعلم أنه من سليمان. وما يعجبني ذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r1.claim: Karīm is said to mean noble because of the sender's nobility.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p324/r2.claim: Another explanation says the letter is noble because it bears a seal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r1.claim: The narrative compresses events: the letter was delivered and read, then the Queen assembled the court.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r1.anchor: في هذا الموضع اختصار لما يدل ظاهر القول عليه تقديره فألقى الكتاب وقرأته وجمعت له أهل ملكها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r2.claim: The “malāʾ” are the leading people who represent everyone else.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r2.anchor: والملأ أشراف الناس الذين ينوبون مناب الجميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the letter was noble because it came from someone great in the Queen’s eyes, honoring Solomon.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r4.claim: A second explanation is that the letter was sealed with a signet; a Prophetic report says a letter’s nobility is its seal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r4.anchor: وإما أنها أشارت إلى أنه مطبوع عليه بالخاتم، وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «كرم الكتاب ختمه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet says a letter is made noble by its seal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r5.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «كرم الكتاب ختمه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.claim: If “noble” means it began with God’s name, the letter is complete rather than deficient; a Prophetic report says speech without the basmala is deficient.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r6.anchor: ف كريم ضد أجذم كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «كل كلام لم يبدأ باسم الله تعالى فهو أجذم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.claim: The letter may reproduce concise, eloquent wording: address first, then God’s name, then a command against arrogance and for submission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r7.anchor: فيحتمل اللفظ أنه نص الكتاب موجزا بليغا وكذلك كتب الأنبياء وقدم فيه العنوان وهي عادة الناس على وجه الدهر، ثم سمى الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.claim: Alternatively, the Queen may have summarized the letter’s meanings rather than its exact sequence, naming Solomon and explaining its message.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p258/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أنها قصدت إلى اقتضاب معانيه دون ترتيبه فأعلمتهم إنه من سليمان وأن معنى ما فيه كذا وكذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r1.claim: Qatada says the hoopoe dropped the letter on the sleeping queen's chest; she read it and informed her people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة أتاها الهدهد وهي نائمة فألقى الكتاب على نحرها فقرأته وأخبرت قومها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r2.claim: Muqatil says the hoopoe carried the letter in its beak, dropped it in her lap, and its seal made her and her troops tremble and submit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل حمله في منقاره حتى وقف على رأس المرأة فرفرف ساعة والناس ينظرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r3.claim: One explanation, transmitted by Said ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, is that the letter was called noble because it was sealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r3.anchor: لأنه كان مختوما رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the queen thought the letter came from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r4.anchor: لانها ظنته من عند الله عز وجل روي عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r5.speaker: قتادة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r5.claim: Qatada and al-Zajjaj say noble means that its contents were good.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r5.anchor: أن معنى قولها كريم حسن ما فيه قاله قتادة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir says it was noble because its sender was a king.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r6.anchor: لكرم صاحبه فانه كان ملكا ذكره ابن جرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r7.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the letter was awe-inspiring.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r7.anchor: لانه كان مهيبا ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r8.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi says it was noble because the hoopoe had been made to carry it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r9.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r9.claim: Al-Tha'labi says the queen saw “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful” at the letter's head.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#3/r9.anchor: لأنها رأت في صدره بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حكاه الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r5.claim: Bilqis was astonished and alarmed, then took the letter, opened its seal, and read it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r5.anchor: فتحيرت مما رأت، وهالها ذلك، ثم عمدت إلى الكتاب فأخذته، ففتحت ختمه وقرأته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r6.claim: Bilqis calls the letter noble because of the wonder of a bird bringing it and withdrawing politely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r6.anchor: تعني بكرمه: ما رأته من عجيب أمره، كون طائر أتى به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r7.claim: Bilqis sees this as something no king could accomplish and beyond their ability.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r7.anchor: وهذا أمر لا يقدر عليه أحد من الملوك، ولا سبيل لهم إلى ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r1.claim: The letter is noble because of its fine content, because it comes from a noble king, or because it is sealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r1.anchor: حسن مضمونة وما فيه ، أو وصفته بالكرم ، لأنه من عند ملك كريم أو مختوم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r2.claim: A prophetic report says that a letter's honor lies in its seal.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r2.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 797 ) ( كرم الكتاب ختمه ) .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r3.claim: When the Prophet wrote to non-Arabs, he was told they would accept only a sealed letter, so he had a signet ring made.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r3.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكتب إلى العجم ، فقيل له : إنهم لا يقبلون إلا كتابا عليه خاتم ، فاصطنع خاتما .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r4.speaker: ابن المقفع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ says that anyone who writes to his brother without sealing the letter has slighted him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن المقفع : من كتب إلى أخيه كتابا ولم يختمه فقد استخف به .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.claim: The basmala resumes and explains the letter's contents: the hearers are told who sent it and what it says.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r5.anchor: قيل : مصدر ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم : هو استئناف وتبيين لما ألقى إليها ، كأنا لما قالت : إني ألقى إلي كتاب كريم ، قيل لها : ممن هو ؟ وما هو ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.claim: An account gives the letter's text from Solomon son of David to Bilqis: greeting to those who follow guidance, followed by a command not to exalt themselves and to come submitting; prophetic letters were concise, scented with musk, and sealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r10.anchor: يروى أن نسخة الكتاب من عبد الله سليمان بن داود إلى بلقيس ملكة سبأ : السلام على من اتبع الهدى ، أما بعد : فلا تعلوا علي وائتوني مسلمين ، وكانت كتب الأنبياء عليهم السلام جملا لا يطيلون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r11.claim: One account says the hoopoe found Bilqis asleep in her palace at Maʾrib, entered through an opening, and dropped the letter on her chest as she lay back with the doors locked and keys beneath her head.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r11.anchor: فوجدها الهدهد راقدة في قصرها بمأرب ، وكانت إذا رقت غلقت الأبواب ووضعت المفاتيح تحت رأسها ، فدخل من كوة وطرح الكتاب على نحرها وهي مستلقية .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r12.claim: Another account says the hoopoe pecked Bilqis awake, frightening her.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r13.claim: A further account has the hoopoe flutter before Bilqis's assembled leaders and soldiers until she looked up, then drop the letter in her lap.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r13.anchor: وقيل : أتاها والقادة والجنود حواليها ، فرفرف ساعة والناس ينظرون حتى رفعت رأسها ، فألقى الكتاب في حجرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r14.claim: Bilqis is described as an Arabic-speaking, literate descendant of Tubbaʿ ibn Sharahil al-Ḥimyarī; seeing the seal, she trembled and submitted before addressing her council.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p367#3/r14.anchor: وكانت قارئة كاتبة عربية من نسل تبع بن شراحيل الحميري ؛ فلما رأت الخاتم ارتعدت وخضعت ، وقالت لقومها ما قالت

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says the queen calls the letter noble because it was sealed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r3.claim: Qatāda says the letter is noble because of its fine contents.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r3.anchor: الثاني : لحسن ما فيه , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r4.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r4.claim: Ibn Baḥr says the letter is noble because its sender was a king.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r4.anchor: الثالث : لكرم صاحبه وأنه كان ملكا , حكاه ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r5.claim: Another possibility is that the hoopoe was made to carry the letter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r6.claim: The author also suggests the letter was noble because it was dropped onto the queen from above.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r6.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : لإلقائه عليها عاليا من نحو السماء

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.claim: The queen was Arab, from the people of Tubbaʿ ibn Abi Sharahil al-Himyari, and her people were Arabs of Tubbaʿ’s people.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.anchor: وكانت عربية من قوم تبع بن أبى شراحيل الحميرى، وقومها من قوم تبع، وهم عرب،

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r9.claim: The queen addresses her nobles and calls Solomon’s letter noble, meaning a fine or excellent letter.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r9.anchor: يعنى الأشراف، { إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم } [آية: 29] يعنى كتاب حسن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r1.claim: The queen addresses her people in a submissive, fearful manner.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r2.claim: The Medinan reading opens the final ya in إني.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r3.claim: A noble letter is handsome in its binding and contents, and sealed.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r4.claim: The Prophet says that a letter’s honor consists in its being sealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r4.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام كرم الكتاب ختمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r5.claim: It is said that whoever receives a brother’s letter without a seal has slighted him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r5.anchor: وقبل من كتب أخيه كتابا ولم يختمه فقد استخف به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r6.claim: The letter is also called noble because it begins with the basmala or comes from a noble king.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#5/r6.anchor: أو مصدر ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r1.claim: The narrative omits that Solomon's messenger delivered the letter, after which Bilqis was heard addressing her council.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r1.anchor: في الكلام حذف والمعنى: فذهب فألقاه إليهم فسمعها وهي تقول: { يأيها الملأ }

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says Bilqis called the letter noble because it came from a great figure in her and her people's estimation, honoring Solomon.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r2.anchor: وهذا قول ابن زيد:. وإما أنها أشارت إلى أنه مطبوع عليه بالخاتم، فكرامة الكتاب ختمه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a speech that does not begin with Bismillah is cut off; some explain noble as referring to the opening formula.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r3.anchor: وقيل: لأنه بدأ فيه ب { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " كل كلام لا يبدأ فيه ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فهو أجذم "

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r4.claim: Other explanations say the letter is noble because Solomon began with himself, because Bilqis thought a bird-carried letter came from heaven, or because noble means beautiful as in the verse about a noble station.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r4.anchor: وقيل: لأنه بدأ فيه بنفسه، ولا يفعل ذلك إلا الجلة. وفي حديث ابن عمر أنه كتب إلى عبد الملك بن مروان يبايعه:

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r5.claim: Qurtubi considers its gentle exhortation to worship God, tactful appeal, and lack of insult or obscure language the best explanation of the noble letter.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r5.anchor: وصفته بذلك لما تضمن من لين القول والموعظة في الدعاء إلى عبادة الله عز وجل، وحسن الاستعطاف والاستلطاف من غير أن يتضمن سبا ولا لعنا،

QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r7.claim: Calling a letter noble is the highest praise; the Qur'an itself is called noble, while people use lesser epithets for letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:29-30/r7.anchor: الوصف بالكريم في الكتاب غاية الوصف ألا ترى قوله تعالى: إنه لقرآن كريم [الواقعة: 77]

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r1.claim: The queen's statement that a letter was delivered to her implicitly omits the hoopoe as the one who threw it to her.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r1.anchor: بمعنى أن يقال إن الهدهد ألقى إليها الكتاب فهو محذوف كأنه ثابت

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r2.claim: One account says the queen locked the doors while sleeping, put the keys under her head, and the hoopoe entered through an opening and laid the letter on her chest; another says he pecked her awake and startled her.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r2.anchor: كانت إذا رقدت غلقت الأبواب ووضعت المفاتيح تحت رأسها فدخل من كوة وطرح الكتاب على نحرها وهي مستلقية

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r3.claim: The letter is called noble because its contents are good, because it came from a noble king, or because it was sealed.

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r4.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r4.claim: A prophetic saying states that a letter's nobility lies in its being sealed.

RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r5.claim: The account says Solomon wrote to non-Arabs and, after being told they accepted only sealed letters, adopted a signet ring.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166#2/r5.anchor: فقيل له إنهم لا يقبلون إلا كتابا عليه خاتم فاتخذ لنفسه خاتما

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

STUDYQURAN:27:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r1.claim: Q and Ṭ offer the letter's seal as one reason the Queen called it noble.
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r1.anchor: called the letter noble either because of its seal, because it was sent by Solomon, or because the contents were noble and good (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:27:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r2.claim: Q and Ṭ also suggest she called the letter noble because Solomon sent it.
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r2.anchor: called the letter noble either because of its seal, because it was sent by Solomon, or because the contents were noble and good (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:27:29/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r3.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r3.claim: Q and Ṭ also suggest its contents were noble and good.
STUDYQURAN:27:29/r3.anchor: called the letter noble either because of its seal, because it was sent by Solomon, or because the contents were noble and good (Q, Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that the hoopoe carried the letter until it was opposite the queen on her throne, then cast it to her.
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم}

TAB-FULL:v18p48/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p48/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p48/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the letter was noble because it came from a king, so its nobility reflected its author’s rank.
TAB-FULL:v18p48/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم}

TABATABAI:27:26-30/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r7.claim: The verse compresses delivery and reading: the hoopoe brings the letter to the queen, she receives and reads it, and then reports it to her council, including how it arrived and what it says.
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r7.anchor: حكاية ذكرها لملإها أمر الكتاب وكيفية وصوله إليها ومضمونه، وقد عظمته إذ وصفته بالكرم

TABATABAI:27:30-31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r5.claim: Other explanations for calling the letter noble are that it was sealed, well written, unusually delivered, or thought to be a heavenly message because a bird brought it; the author finds these conjectural and unconvincing.
TABATABAI:27:30-31/r5.anchor: فقيل وجه كرامته أنه كان مختوما ففي الحديث إكرام الكتاب ختمه حتى ادعى بعضهم أن معنى كرامة الكتاب ختمه

ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r3.claim: The account omits the hoopoe’s going and delivering the letter because the context makes that action clear.

ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p117/r4.claim: كتاب كريم means that the letter contains good things.

TABRISI:27:27-31/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r8.claim: The narrative omits that the hoopoe went, delivered the letter, and Belqīs then saw it.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره. فمضى الهدهد بالكتاب وألقاه إليهم فلما رأته بلقيس

TABRISI:27:27-31/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r9.claim: Belqīs addresses the nobles by calling them the assembly.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r9.anchor: قالت } لقومها { يا أيها الملأ } أي الأشراف

TABRISI:27:27-31/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:27:27-31/r10.claim: Qatāda says the hoopoe arrived while Belqīs lay asleep on her back, dropped the letter on her chest, and she read it.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: أتاها الهدهد وهي نائمة مستلقية على قفاها فألقى الكتاب على نحرها فقرأت الكتاب

TABRISI:27:27-31/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r11.speaker: وهب وابن زيد
TABRISI:27:27-31/r11.claim: In another account, a sun-facing window prompted Belqīs to prostrate at sunrise; the hoopoe blocked it with his wing, and then threw the letter to her.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r11.anchor: وقيل: كانت لها كوة مستقبلة للشمس تقع الشمس عندما تطلع فيها فإذا نظرت إليها سجدت

TABRISI:27:27-31/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r12.speaker: وهب وابن زيد
TABRISI:27:27-31/r12.claim: The window account continues that the hoopoe blocked the sunlight, causing Belqīs to rise and look before he cast the letter to her.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r12.anchor: فجاء الهدهد إلى الكوة فسدها بجناحه فارتفعت الشمس ولم تعلم فقامت تنظر فرمى الكتاب إليها عن وهب وابن زيد

TABRISI:27:27-31/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r13.claim: After taking the letter, Belqīs gathered the nobles, who numbered 310 rulers.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r13.anchor: فلما أخذت الكتاب جمعت الأشراف وهم يومئذ ثلاثمائة عشر قيلا

TABRISI:27:27-31/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:27:27-31/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says she called the letter noble because it was sealed; a report says sealing a letter honors it.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r14.anchor:
سمته كريما لأنه كان مختوما عن ابن عباس ويؤيده الحديث:
" إكرام الكتاب ختمه

TABRISI:27:27-31/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:27:27-31/r15.claim: Other explanations are that the letter was noble because it began with the basmala, because its handwriting and wording were excellent, or because Solomon ruled humans, jinn, and birds and had exalted kingship.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r15.anchor: وقيل: وصفته بالكريم لأنه صدره ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم.

TABRISI:27:27-31/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:27:27-31/r16.claim: One explanation of the letter's nobility is its beautiful handwriting, excellent wording, and eloquence.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r16.anchor: وقيل: لحسن خطه وجودة لفظه وبيانه.

TABRISI:27:27-31/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:27:27-31/r17.claim: She may have called it noble because Solomon ruled humans, jinn, and birds and was famed for high and mighty kingship.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r17.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كان ممن يملك الإنس والجن والطير وقد كانت سمعت بخبر سليمان فسمته كريما

THALABI:v7p205/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r1.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والثمالي
THALABI:v7p205/r1.claim: They report that Belqis's council had 313 members, each overseeing ten thousand men.
THALABI:v7p205/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل والثمالي: كان أهل مشورتها ثلاثمائة وثلاثة عشر رجلا كل رجل منهم على عشرة آلاف

THALABI:v7p205/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p205/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the letter's being noble as its being good, comparing it with the Qurʾānic phrase about an honorable station.
THALABI:v7p205/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: حسن، نظيره قوله ومقام كريم .

THALABI:v7p205/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p205/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the letter was noble because of the honor of its sender.
THALABI:v7p205/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: شريف بشرف صاحبه.

THALABI:v7p205/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r4.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v7p205/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the letter was called noble because it was sealed.
THALABI:v7p205/r4.anchor: الضحاك: سمته كريما لأنه كان مختوما

THALABI:v7p205/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p205/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet the saying that a letter's seal is its mark of honor.
THALABI:v7p205/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «كرامة الكتاب ختمه» .

THALABI:v7p205/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r6.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v7p205/r6.claim: Anas reports that when the Prophet was to write to non-Arabs, he was told they accept only sealed letters; he made a seal, whose whiteness Anas recalls seeing in his palm.
THALABI:v7p205/r6.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس قال: لما أراد نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكتب إلى العجم

THALABI:v7p205/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r7.speaker: ابن المقفع
THALABI:v7p205/r7.claim: Ibn al-Muqaffa says an unsealed letter to a friend shows contempt, since a seal is what completes a letter.
THALABI:v7p205/r7.anchor: وقال ابن المقفع: من كتب الى أخيه كتابا ولم يختمه فقد استخف به لأن الختم ختم

THALABI:v7p205/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p205/r8.speaker: قول غير مسمى
THALABI:v7p205/r8.claim: An unnamed explanation says the letter was noble because it began with In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
THALABI:v7p205/r8.anchor: وقيل: سمته كريما لأنه كان مصدرا ب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r1.claim: The implied sequence is that the hoopoe went and delivered the letter to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: تقدير الكلام: فمضى الهدهد فألقى الكتاب إليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the hoopoe found the queen asleep on her back and dropped the letter on her neck.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: أتاها الهدهد وهي نائمة مستلقية على قفاها فألقى الكتاب على نحرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says the hoopoe perched above her, flapped as people watched, then dropped the letter in her lap when she raised her head.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أتاها الهدهد حتى وقف على رأسها فرفرف ساعة، والناس ينظرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r4.claim: Muqatil's account identifies the queen as an Arab of the people of Tubba al-Himyari.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r4.anchor: وكانت عربية من قوم: تبع الحميري، فأخبرت قومها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r5.claim: They gloss “noble letter” as stamped or sealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r5.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: مطبوع (¬5). وهو: قول الضحاك قال: سمته كريما؛ لأنه كان مختوما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r6.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's saying that a letter's honor lies in its seal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r6.anchor: ويدل عليه ما روى ابن عباس: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "كرامة الكتاب ختمه"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r7.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r7.claim: Qatada and Muqatil understand the description as meaning that the letter was good.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers “good,” explaining that the letter's contents were good; he connects this sense to the “pleasant station” in 26:58 and 44:26.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r8.anchor: وهو اختيار الزجاج، قال: حسن ما فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r9.claim: It is also said that she called the letter noble because its sender was noble: she recognized a king's letter delivered by a bird.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r9.anchor: ويقال: سمته كريما لكرم صاحبه؛ وذلك أنها رأت # كتاب ملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the letter as honorable through the honor of its sender.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p220#2/r10.anchor: وهذا معنى ما روي عن ابن عباس: شريف، بشرف صاحبه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r2.claim: The queen calls the letter noble because its contents are good.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r2.anchor: كتاب كريم } حسن ما فيه، ثم بينت ما فيه فقالت:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.claim: Qatāda relates that Bilqīs, daughter of Sharāḥbīl, was a Yemeni woman from a royal household; after her people died, she became their ruler.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: ذكر لنا أنها امرأة من أهل اليمن كانت في بيت مملكة، يقال لها بلقيس ابنة شرحبيل، فهلك قومها، فملكت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.claim: Abū Bakra reports that the Prophet said a people ruled by a woman will not prosper.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.anchor: وحدثني المبارك، عن الحسن، عن أبي بكرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لن يفلح قوم تملكهم امرأة» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.claim: Qatāda says Bilqīs locked the doors, put the keys under her head, and went to bed; the hoopoe entered through an opening and dropped the letter on her belly or between her breasts, where she found it and read it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.anchor: سعيد، قال قتادة: وأنها كانت إذا رقدت غلقت الأبواب، وأخذت المفاتيح فوضعتها تحت رأسها، فلما غلقت الأبواب وآوت إلى فراشها أتاها الهدهد حتى دخل من كوة بيتها، فقذف الصحيفة على بطنها أو بين ثدييها، فأخذت الصحيفة فقرأتها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r5.claim: Al-Suddī explains “a noble letter” as a good letter with good contents.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r5.anchor: فقرأتها ف {قالت يأيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم} [النمل: 29] أي: ، حسن، حسن ما فيه، تفسير السدي.

DAMGHANI:v1p401/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p401/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p401/r14.claim: The entry also lists كريم in one's own estimation, forbearance, and excellence among its senses.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.claim: The first Quranic sense is excellence or superiority, including God’s honoring Adam’s children and the noble book, messenger, and person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكريم في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r2.claim: The letter is noble because of its writer, Solomon; it may also be called noble because it is sealed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r2.anchor: وقال: إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم [النمل: 29] أي شريف لشرف كاتبه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r1.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ criticizes writers on Qurʾānic inimitability for taking polemical detours into proliferating arguments and contentious technicalities instead of a sound path of inquiry.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r1.anchor: بيد أنهم يمرون فى ذلك عُرضا على غير طريق، وويشتقون فى الكلام ههنا وههنا من كل ما تمترس به الألسنة فى اللدد والخصومة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r2.speaker: الرافعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r2.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī conjectures that al-Jāḥiẓ's lost book on inimitability only began affirming eloquence, since it preceded the formation of rhetoric as a discipline; Bint criticizes his conjectural method.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r2.anchor: والرافعى لا يتحرج من القول بالظن فى مصنفات السلف: فهر يحكم على كتاب الجاحظ، ولم يصل إلينا، بأنه لم يحاول فيه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r3.speaker: الرافعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r3.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī conjectures that al-Wāsiṭī built on al-Jāḥiẓ and that ʿAbd al-Qāhir built his Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz on al-Wāsiṭī, although both earlier books are lost.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r3.anchor: ولا نظن الواسطى بنى إلا على ما ابتدأه الجاحظ، كما بنى عبد القاهر فى دلائل الإعجاز على الواسطى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r4.speaker: الرافعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r4.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī dismisses Ibn Suraqa's lost book with the inference that a useful work would have survived; Bint presents this as another unsupported judgment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r4.anchor: فيحكم عليه قائلا: "على أن كتابه لوكان مما ينفع الناس لمكث فى الأرض

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r5.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī first treated inimitability within Tārīkh Ādāb al-ʿArab, then issued it as a separate book to make it useful and accessible.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r5.anchor: ثم أفرده مستقلا ليكون كما قال: (كتابا بنفسه، تعم به المنفعة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r6.claim: Bint says al-Rāfiʿī could not tolerate contemporary disagreement over his book and notes that some supporters praised it in extravagant, quasi-revelatory terms.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p30/r6.anchor: ولم يحتمل - رحمه الله - أن يختلف معاصروه فى كتابه، فيكون منهم من يراه فصل الخطاب وشهد له بأنه كأنه تنزيل من التنزيل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.claim: He calls this fā the explicative fā that signals omitted but understood events, as in the unspoken striking of the stone, the steps after the command to go, and the Hudhud’s delivery of Solomon’s letter.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.anchor: هذه الفاء إذن هي فاء الفصيحة التي تدلّ على أن هناك محذوف ولكن المعنى واضح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.claim: In Solomon’s story, the text omits the hoopoe taking the letter, carrying and dropping it by Bilqis, and waiting; the meaning remains clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.anchor: المفروض أن الهدهد أخذ الكتاب وذهب به وألقاه عند بلقيس وانتظر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.claim: Ibn Mujāhid counts 27 possessive yāʾs in the sūra, six disputed; the excerpt names the first four locations.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.anchor: ياءات الإضافة فى هذه السورة سبع وعشرون ياء إضافة اختلفوا فى ست منهن ﴿ آنست نارا ﴾

NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.speaker: نافع، أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Ja'far open the speaker yāʾ in the ten listed loci, including 11:54 and 27:29; the other loci are in 3:36, 5:29, 5:115, 6:14, 7:156, 28:27 and 39:12.
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.anchor: ففتح الياء فيهن نافع وأبو جعفر إلا أني أوفي فإنه اختلف فيها عن أبي جعفر

NASHR:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r2.claim: The fifth class has a ḍamma then kasra and 22 agreed occurrences, including ولا يأب الشهداء إذا and الفقراء إلى الله; six occurrences differ, including Maryam’s يا ذكرياء إنا and five addresses to the Prophet attributed to Nafi.

NASHR:v1p453/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p453/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p453/r1.claim: The rasm adds an alif after wāw in these three Naml instances of الملأ, by analogy with the alif after wāw of a pronoun.
NASHR:v1p453/r1.anchor: وزيدت الألف بعد الواو في هذه المواضع تشبيها بالألف الواقعة بعد واو الضمير

NASHR:v1p453/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p453/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p453/r4.claim: A final hamza written as wāw when rounded or yāʾ when kasra signals eased pronunciation at pause; the author prefers this over proposals that writing strengthens the hamza, shows its vowel, or treats it as medial when connected.
NASHR:v1p453/r4.anchor: والأول هو الصواب؛ لظهور فائدته وبيان ثمرته

NASHR:v2p340/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p340/r5.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p340/r5.claim: The two Medinan readers open the yāʾ in إني ألقي.
NASHR:v2p340/r5.anchor: إني ألقي، ليبلوني أأشكر فتحهما المدنيان
